source: K0 conversion to E4, derived from K3-K28, their prerequisite/composes edges, bundles, M0/M1/M2 and tools. Q1-Q3 are controls the current K0 answers. Key reviewed by a fresh agent before any reader ran; Q5 (K17 a SysML-only near miss), Q2, Q4 and Q6 corrected.

probes.question: Why is each skill two files - a K stub in skills/ and a SKILL.md in its own directory?
probes.key: The stub is the catalogue entry (id, status, title, hydration trigger) and points at the body; the body carries none of those, so it stays portable - a foreign catalogue id would make it unusable elsewhere. SC3 governs the body, SC1 the stub.
probes.rubric: 2 for the stub as catalogue entry and the body kept portable. 1 for one half. 0 otherwise.

probes.question: Someone proposes naming skills by level - l1-, l2- - to show which build on which. What does the corpus say?
probes.key: No: composition is declared as edges (prerequisite, composes) in each SKILL.md frontmatter and depth is derived as the longest path; a level in the name freezes a graph that is expected to change. skill-graph.mjs checks the edges.
probes.rubric: 2 for no, with edges and derived depth. 1 for no alone. 0 otherwise.

probes.question: A document describes how to run a review but has no scripts or assets and is meant to be read, not executed. Is it a skill?
probes.key: No: a skill is invoked and executed largely as written, earning its packaging where scripts or assets make it necessary; descriptive guidance is a method, rule or practice.
probes.rubric: 2 for no, routed to method (or rule/practice). 1 for no alone. 0 otherwise.

probes.question: What would an unhealthy population of skills look like?
probes.key: Any two population faults: a stub without a body or a body without a stub; levels encoded in names; one family growing while whole kinds of capability have none; two skills packaging one procedure; skills that only work inside one host's coordination system with no neutral counterpart; descriptive guidance filed as skills. A single skill's narrated body is a member defect.
probes.rubric: 2 for two population faults. 1 for one. 0 for none, or only a single skill's defect.
